identity.title: ALMA resolves turbulent, rotating [CII] emission in a young starburst galaxy at z = 4.8

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper, we present new ALMA observations which spatially resolve the [Cii] emission around an SMG at $z=$ 4.76 in the Extended *Chandra* Deep Field South (ECDFS): ALESS 73.1

distance_source.value: [CII] redshift from these ALMA data; H0=73, Om=0.27, OL=0.73, 6.4 kpc/arcsec

question.value: What are the spatial distribution and kinematics of [CII] and rest-frame far-infrared emission in the z=4.76 SMG ALESS 73.1, and what do they imply for its dynamical mass, stability and metallicity?

evidence.quote: Our new ALMA observations map the spatial distribution and kinematics of the [Cii] and rest-frame far-infrared emission within this system on $\sim$ kpc scales
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00124.S.
We used the Band 7 receivers with the four basebands centered at 317.20, 319.07, 329.54, and 331.11 GHz.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four basebands at 317.20, 319.07, 329.54, 331.11 GHz; [CII] in the last two; 1875 MHz per baseband, 488.28 kHz x 3840 channels

evidence.quote: The correlator was used in the frequency domain mode with a bandwidth of 1875 MHz (488.28 kHz $\times$ 3840 channels per baseband).
The [Cii] $\lambda$157.74 $\mu$m line is a powerful alternative line to $^{12}$CO
in the compact Cycle 0 configuration, with 23 antennas covering baselines between 18 m and 402 m
with 23 antennas covering baselines between 18 m and 402 m
cleaned it using natural weighting, which provides a final synthesized beam size of 0.65$''$ $\times$ 0.40$''$ at position angle of 91$^{\circ}$

sensitivity.value: continuum rms 0.15 mJy in combined map

evidence.quote: We also made a combined 318.13 + 330.34 GHz continuum map, which reaches an rms noise level of 0.15 mJy.
The total time on target was 1.62 h.
The ALMA observations of ALESS 73.1 were obtained on UT 2012 July 18 and 27

method.value: CASA reduction, natural-weighted cube binned to 24.85 km/s; continuum from line-free channels

evidence.quote: The data reduction followed the standard procedures in the Common Astronomy Software Applications (casa) package (cite: petry12).

analysis_steps.goal: Fit velocity field with rotating disk

method.value: Single-Gaussian velocity field fit, then thin exponential-disk dynamical model convolved with beam

evidence.quote: We fit the velocity field with a dynamical model assuming that the ionised gas is circularly rotating in a thin disk

assumptions.value: exponential surface density, hydrodynamical effects neglected

evidence.quote: We neglect all hydrodynamical effects, therefore the disk motion is entirely determined by the gravitational potential.

validation.value: Compared with KinMS and arctan models giving similar results

evidence.quote: Both the alternative models, which have significantly different flux distributions from the model described above, obtain similar results.

method.value: M_dyn sin^2 i = R v^2/G with MCMC (1e5 realisations) over disk parameters; range from three models

evidence.quote: we use a Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) with 10$^5$ realisations to investigate the uncertainties on the disk model parameters
To constrain the inclination, we use a Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) with 10$^5$ realisations to investigate the uncertainties on the disk model parameters

method.value: Q = sqrt2 sigma V /(pi r G Sigma) per pixel using [CII] luminosity as proxy for Sigma, flat rotation curve

evidence.quote: using the [Cii] luminosity distribution as a proxy to determine $\Sigma$
We therefore assume that the [Cii] emission traces well the kinematics of the underlying star-forming molecular gas component

analysis_steps.goal: Gas, stellar mass, alpha_CO, outflow limit

method.value: Atomic gas mass from Hailey-Dunsheath eq. 1; mass budget; outflow from forced broad Gaussian component

evidence.quote: we fitted the ALMA spectrum by forcing an additional broad component with a fwhm $>$ 500 km s$^{-1}$

evidence.quote: a critical density $n_{\rm crit}$=2.7$\times$10$^3$ cm$^{-3}$ and a PDR surface temperature $\sim$300 K
The data reduction followed the standard procedures in the Common Astronomy Software Applications (casa) package (cite: petry12).

findings_qualitative.value: [CII] disk extends about twice as far as the dust continuum and shows rotation

evidence.quote: the [Cii] emitting gas extends twice as far out as the dust continuum

claims.hypothesis: Is the [CII] emission in ALESS 73.1 a rotating disk?
claims.experiment: Dynamical modelling of the velocity field with three models

evidence.quote: implying that this is a highly turbulent rotating disk

claims.hypothesis: Is the gas disk gravitationally stable?
claims.finding: Disk unstable throughout, can fuel the starburst

evidence.quote: At all radii, $Q$ is well below 1, suggesting that the disk is unstable throughout.

claims.hypothesis: Is the galaxy low in stellar mass and gas rich?
claims.experiment: Mass budget from M_dyn, M_a, M_H2
claims.finding: First major burst of star formation

evidence.quote: suggests we are observing its first major burst of star formation

claims.hypothesis: Is the metallicity close to solar?

evidence.quote: As such, subsolar metallicities are still possible in ALESS73.1.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Stellar-dominated SED excluded due to light-to-mass ratio

evidence.quote: We therefore exclude the possibility that the SED is dominated by stellar emission.

limitations_admitted.value: Disk barely resolved so flux distribution and dynamical mass uncertain

evidence.quote: as we barely spatially resolve the flux distribution within the disk, we cannot distinguish which flux distribution is more appropriate
